design: RCT, POST HOC analysis
justification: Parent trial (Frias 2018) was adequately randomised and double blind, and biomarkers were measured by immunoassay at central laboratories, so D1, D2 and D4 are low. D3 some concerns: analysis required non-missing baseline and at least one post-baseline value, and stored sample availability governed inclusion. D5 HIGH: the authors state plainly that sample sizes were based on the parent trial's primary endpoints rather than prespecified biomarker analyses, and that this was a post hoc analysis without a prepublished protocol. Ten biomarkers were measured and reported selectively in the narrative. All authors are Eli Lilly employees and shareholders. Overall HIGH, driven by D5.

design: RCT, POST HOC analysis

D3 some concerns given analysis-set definitions. Five of six authors are Boehringer Ingelheim employees. Overall HIGH.

design: RCT, phase 2a
justification: Randomised double blind placebo controlled phase 2a. Liver fat by MRI-PDFF is an objective centrally read outcome, so D4 low. D5 some concerns: liver fat was a prespecified endpoint of this substudy, which is better than the post hoc analyses above, but the four dose arms share a single placebo arm of n=19 and selective dose-arm emphasis is possible. Eli Lilly funded.

design: RCT, secondary analysis
justification: D2 HIGH: open label design, which for a weight-sensitive biomarker in an active comparator trial permits differential co-intervention. The authors themselves note the open label design as a limitation and report differential use of new antihypertensive and lipid lowering medication between arms. D3 some concerns: 174 of 515 exenatide and 128 of 514 glimepiride patients discontinued, differential attrition, and patients failing glycaemic control exited the study, which the authors note may have selected for responders. D5 some concerns: hsCRP was a secondary endpoint among many cardiovascular risk markers. Note this trial is ACTIVE CONTROLLED and is excluded from Q2 class contrasts regardless of its risk of bias. Amylin and Eli Lilly funded.

design: RCT, prespecified secondary endpoints
justification: Multicentre double blind placebo controlled trial, 171 randomised after an 8 month open label metformin run-in. D1 some concerns: randomisation by drawing of envelopes containing codes prepared by a statistician, allocation concealment not described. D2 low: matched placebo injections, double blind. D3 low: 11 of 171 withdrew (6 per cent), intention to treat with at least one post randomisation measure. D4 some concerns: assay sites and blinding of laboratory staff not stated, and the 12 month SDs are implausibly small against baseline (hsCRP 0.2 and 0.4 against 0.8 mg/l, fasting insulin 0.2 against 42 pmol/l), which is a reporting accuracy concern rather than evidence of bias. D5 some concerns: no registration or protocol cited; inflammation markers named as secondary endpoints in Methods; the authors report hsCRP and TNF-alpha as not different between groups by ANCOVA. No industry funding declared. Overall some concerns; the variance reporting is flagged for the sensitivity analyses.

design: RCT, pilot, biomarkers as stated aim

D5 some concerns: no registration or protocol; inflammatory and oxidative markers are the stated aim of the pilot but no sample size calculation and multiple markers reported; between group hsCRP result supported by ANCOVA. Eli Lilly supplied drug and an unrestricted grant; authors declare no competing financial interests. Overall some concerns; n = 23 and very low baseline hsCRP (0.4 and 0.6 mg/L) limit the precision of any contrast.

design: RCT, crossover, exploratory secondary analysis
justification: AddHope2 investigator initiated double blind placebo controlled crossover trial, 12 + 12 weeks, protocol published (BMJ Open 2014). D3 high: 13 of 41 randomised did not complete (32 per cent), dropout concentrated during liraglutide (gastrointestinal), ITT uses whatever data were available. D4 low: hsCRP and TNF-alpha by ELISA with reported CVs. D5 high: the authors state that lipoprotein density and low grade inflammation were not predefined outcomes of the AddHope2 trial and describe the analysis as explorative with a risk of false positives; post hoc power analysis only. Novo Nordisk unrestricted grant; several authors with Novo Nordisk ties. Overall high, driven by D3 and D5. Placebo controlled, eligible for Q2.

design: RCT, CRP as secondary laboratory variable

D2 low: double blind, intention to treat with last observation carried forward, 23 of 24 completed. D3 low. D4 low: hospital biochemistry laboratory, blinded. D5 some concerns: CRP is a secondary laboratory variable rather than a registered endpoint; one liraglutide CRP value above 5 mg/dL was excluded as acute infection after unblinding. Novo Nordisk funded and supplied drug; investigators controlled analysis and reporting. Overall some concerns. Listed as Wagner 2019 in Alrasheed 2026.

design: 26 week open label active controlled parallel group multicentre trial, add on liraglutide versus sitagliptin versus insulin glargine on metformin, 75 patients with type 2 diabetes and NAFLD, intention
justification: S: randomised 1:1:1 across 10 centres with balanced baseline characteristics (D1 low); open label, and the comparator is titrated basal insulin, so behaviour and dose adjustment differ by arm without blinding (D2 high); intention to treat with 65 of 75 completing and non completers classified as having no improvement for the imaging endpoints, a conservative but non standard imputation (D3 some concerns); MRI IDEAL IQ and central laboratory measures (D4 low); registered trial with its prespecified primary (intrahepatic lipid) and the full table of secondary endpoints reported (D5 low)

design: randomised double blind placebo controlled phase 2 trial, semaglutide 2.4 mg versus placebo for 48 weeks in biopsy confirmed NASH related cirrhosis, 71 patients randomised 2:1
justification: S: randomised 2:1 by an interactive web response system stratified by diabetes status (D1 low); double blind with a visually matching placebo (D2 low); 64 of 71 completed treatment with 63 evaluable paired biopsies and the full analysis set used (D3 low); histology read centrally by one blinded pathologist and imaging and laboratory measures central (D4 low); registered trial reporting its prespecified primary (which was null and in the unfavourable direction) and its secondary endpoints (D5 low)

design: single centre randomised open label controlled trial, exenatide twice daily versus insulin aspart 30 twice daily, 66 patients with type 2 diabetes, 52 weeks, carotid intima media thickness primary
justification: S: randomised 1:1 but with a sex imbalance (19 of 27 men versus 14 of 32, p 0.038) and a 5 mmHg diastolic difference at baseline (D1 some concerns); open label comparison of an injected incretin with twice daily premixed insulin (D2 high); 66 randomised and 59 in the full analysis set without a flow account in this report (D3 some concerns); laboratory and ultrasound measures with blinded reading of the primary (D4 low); the inventory markers are secondary to a carotid imaging primary, and Table 1 contains an evident copy error in the LDL row (D5 some concerns)

design: open label randomised study, semaglutide added to maximally tolerated metformin versus metformin alone for 12 weeks, 31 patients with plaque psoriasis and type 2 diabetes
justification: S: described as randomised but the groups are defined by whether patients were assigned semaglutide, with no sequence, concealment or allocation ratio described and a threefold difference in baseline CRP between arms (3.8 against 9.6 mg/L) in 31 patients (D1 high); open label with no placebo and the comparator arm simply continuing metformin (D2 high); no account of withdrawals (D3 some concerns); dermatological scoring by unblinded assessors, laboratory measures unblinded (D4 some concerns); the metabolic markers are secondary to the skin endpoint and are reported as a mixture of means and medians without a between arm comparison (D5 some concerns)

design: biomarker analysis of a phase 3 randomised double blind placebo controlled trial of tirzepatide 5, 10 or 15 mg for 72 weeks in obesity without diabetes, in 392 of the randomly selected completers
justification: S: the parent trial is randomised and double blind with a matched placebo (D1 and D2 low); the biomarker set is restricted to 100 randomly selected completers per group and 392 after sample volume exclusions, so it is a non random subset of the randomised population in one respect (completion) although the selection within completers was random (D3 some concerns); central assays of stored plasma on a mixed model of log transformed values (D4 low); these are exploratory biomarkers outside the parent protocol's endpoints, and five of the inventory markers are reported with point estimates whose intervals sit in a supplement (D5 some concerns)

design: double blind placebo controlled randomised trial, liraglutide 1.8 mg added to multiple daily insulin injections versus placebo, 122 randomised with type 2 diabetes, 24 weeks
justification: S: randomised with a matched placebo in a double blind design (D1 and D2 low); 122 of 124 enrolled had at least one valid follow up and the analysis reports n per cell (D3 low); laboratory adiponectin and calibrated scales with a single scale per patient (D4 low); adiponectin is a secondary endpoint of an anthropometric report, and the baseline predictors of its change are explored post hoc (D5 some concerns)

design: 40 week multicentre randomised double blind placebo controlled trial of tirzepatide monotherapy 5, 10 or 15 mg in type 2 diabetes, 478 randomised, ITT efficacy analysis set
justification: S: randomised 1:1:1:1 through an interactive web response system and double blind with a volume matched placebo (D1 and D2 low); the ITT efficacy analysis set is reported with n per arm and the primary publication accounts for the flow (D3 low); central laboratory assays with standard errors on a mixed model (D4 low); these are secondary and exploratory beta cell endpoints of a trial powered for HbA1c (D5 some concerns)

design: randomised double blind placebo controlled phase 2 trial, mazdutide 3, 4.5 or 6 mg versus placebo for 24 weeks in Chinese overweight adults or adults with obesity, 248 randomised
justification: S: randomised with a stratification factor and double blind against placebo (D1 and D2 low); 224 of 248 completed and missing week 24 data for the primary endpoint were imputed by last observation carried forward, with the secondary endpoints on a mixed model (D3 some concerns); central laboratory assays (D4 low); this is an interim analysis of the low dose part of a two part trial, and the cardiometabolic markers are secondary endpoints with no multiplicity adjustment, as the table states (D5 some concerns)
